EdgeProp Singapore recognises top-performing property agents at the third Realtors’ Roundtable
article:
For many Singaporeans, buying or selling a property is one of the most significant financial decisions they make. In an increasingly complex property market, choosing the right adviser is just as important as choosing the right property.

EdgeProp Singapore has presented the third edition of its Realtors’ Roundtable (RRT), an independent platform established to help consumers identify trusted real estate professionals based on performance, professionalism and client service.

“With so much data, technology and artificial intelligence available, where does the value of a property agent come from? I believe the answer is trust,” says Bernard Tong, CEO of EdgeProp.

“A trusted professional gives people confidence,” he adds.

Now in its third year, the Realtors’ Roundtable continues to recognise real estate professionals who have consistently demonstrated strong performance, professionalism and a commitment to client service. With more than 36,000 registered real estate salespersons in Singapore, only a select group qualifies for the Realtors' Roundtable each year.

Eligibility is determined by a realtor's production, comprising commission and overriding commission earned during the qualifying period. Strong and consistent production is one indicator of a proven track record in helping clients achieve their property goals, while overriding commission also recognises those who mentor and develop their teams.

To ensure the integrity of the recognition, applicants are required to submit their commission and overriding income for assessment. The figures are verified with their respective agencies or against their official income statements, before undergoing a second round of independent verification by the Official Knowledge Partner, KPMG Singapore.

Members are recognised across three qualification tiers based on their production during the assessment period.

Based on production between 1 Jan 2025 and 31 Dec 2025, expressed in local currency. Production is defined as total commission and overriding received, excluding deductibles (agency cut and GST) and basic income.

Beyond annual performance, this year's Realtors’ Roundtable also recognises sustained excellence and emerging talent within the profession.

This year's event introduces three new accolades. The RRT Milestone Award is presented to members who have qualified for the Realtors' Roundtable for three consecutive years, while the RRT Titan Award is presented to members who have maintained their Millionaire Member status for three consecutive years.

The event also continues to recognise emerging talent through the RRT Young Achiever Award, presented to Realtors’ Roundtable members aged 30 or below (based on the calendar year). The award celebrates young real estate professionals who have achieved outstanding sales performance early in their careers while meeting the rigorous qualifying criteria.

A total of 425 real estate professionals qualified for this year's Realtors' Roundtable, comprising 230 members from Singapore and 195 members from Malaysia. In Singapore, the number of qualified members increased by 62% year-on-year, underscoring the Realtors’ Roundtable’s growing recognition and the increasing number of real estate professionals meeting its rigorous qualifying standards.

The event was supported by partners McLaren Singapore, Anthony Law Corporation, The Assembly Place, Makeover Inc, LytePay and Circular Law Chambers, as well as supporting agencies across Singapore and Malaysia.

The full list of 2026 Realtors' Roundtable members is available below. For more information, please visit https://www.realtorsrt.com/

About Realtors' Roundtable

Realtors' Roundtable (RRT) is an independent platform by EdgeProp Singapore that recognises outstanding real estate professionals who demonstrate excellence in performance, professionalism and client service.

title: UOL readies mega Thomson Reserve condo launch in 4Q2026, and luxury NoMad Hilton hotel debut
article:
The 1,268-unit Thomson Reserve residential development — a joint venture (JV) between UOL Group and CapitaLand Development — will be launched for sale in the fourth quarter of 2026.

Following which, the debuts of the Dorset Gardens condo and the Hougang Central landmark mixed-use development are both slated for 2027.

UOL's solid launch pipeline follows recent strong sales momentum from property development, across Singapore projects such as Watten House , Pinetree Hill , Meyer Blue , Skye at Holland , UpperHouse at Orchard Boulevard , and ParkTown Residence .

Those projects, in which UOL has a 90% effective stake, are between 79% and 100% sold as at Aug 9, the property and hospitality group said in its 1H2026 financial results announcement on Aug 12.

Higher operating profits from property development and property investments drove a 16% y-o-y increase in UOL’s attributable profit before fair value and other gains (operating Patmi) to $239.8 million for the first half of this year.

UOL noted that its projects' resilient sales performance comes as Singapore's residential market has been supported by healthy demand-supply dynamics and strong household balance sheets. The company expects new home sales to remain stable.

"Demand for quality homes in good locations has remained healthy, with buyers continuing to gravitate towards new launches that offer strong connectivity and comprehensive amenities," said Liam Wee Sin, UOL group CEO.

"This gives us confidence as we prepare for the launch of Thomson Reserve, our next residential development," he added.

Upcoming residential launches

Thomson Reserve, a high-profile mega development that will rise on the site of the former Thomson View condo along Bright Hill Drive, is set to launch in 4Q2026.

It is a 50:50 JV between UOL Group and CapitaLand Development.

Sitting on a 51,567 sq m (555,063 sq ft) leasehold site, it will comprise 1,268 residences, ranging from two-bedroom to five-bedroom units.

UOL and CapitaLand's $810 million en bloc purchase of Thomson View, first announced in October 2024, was completed in October 2025.

Located next to Upper Thomson MRT Station and within 1km of Ai Tong School, the new condo is expected to offer panoramic views of MacRitchie Reservoir, Windsor Nature Park, and the Lower and Upper Peirce Reservoirs.

Also in the pipeline is the Dorset Gardens project, which will feature two 28-storey residential towers with about 428 units and is targeted for launch in the first half of 2027.

An 80:20 JV between UOL Group and Kheng Leong, the project will sit on a 10,399 sq m leasehold government land sale (GLS) site. The consortium was awarded the site after having submitted the top bid of $1,338 psf per plot ratio (ppr) or $524.3 million, out of nine bids, last October.

The upcoming Dorset Gardens condo will be located along Dorset Road in District 8 in the city fringe, next to Farrer Park MRT Station and popular schools such as St Joseph’s Institution.

Meanwhile, in the second half of 2027, the Hougang Central project is expected to launch.

Situated on a 46,899 sq m leasehold site, the mixed-use development will have more than 800 residential units with about 28,000 sq m of commercial space.

It will also be integrated with Hougang MRT Station and the new bus interchange and town plaza.

The residential component is a 40:10:50 JV between UOL Group, Kheng Leong and CapitaLand Development. The commercial component is fully owned by CapitaLand Integrated Commercial Trust.

The consortium clinched the GLS site this January for about $1.5 billion or a land rate of $1,179 psf ppr.

Marina Square revamp and The Clifford redevelopment

As for its property investments, UOL is looking to partially redevelop the Marina Square complex, which comprises Marina Square shopping mall, Pan Pacific Singapore, Parkroyal Collection Marina Bay, and Mandarin Oriental, Singapore.

In its Aug 12 bourse filing, UOL said it will likely provide updates on the timeline by the third quarter of 2026. That is when it expects to obtain the Written Permission for the Strategic Development Incentive (SDI) Scheme.

The company had submitted the revised proposal in 2H2025 to URA to transform the Marina Square complex , with the addition of three buildings — a residential tower, a serviced apartment block, and a mixed-use tower with hospitality, office, and performing arts spaces.

Meanwhile, The Clifford at Raffles Place is slated for completion in 2028.

It is a redevelopment of the former Clifford Centre into a new 35-storey commercial office tower with net lettable area spanning more than 405,000 sq ft of premium Grade A office space, retail and lifestyle amenities.

Steady hospitality performance

In the hospitality sector, UOL reported resilient operating performance for the first half of 2026.

Occupancy for owned hotels was stable at 77% in Singapore (unchanged from 1H2025), up slightly to 74% in Oceania (from 72% previously), and also edging up to 68% in other markets such as China, Vietnam, Malaysia, Myanmar, Indonesia and the UK (from 66% previously).

Revenue per available room (RevPAR) also went up on a y-o-y basis in each market: $293 in Singapore (from $291), $170 in Oceania (from $160), and $122 in other markets (from $115).

UOL expects Singapore's hospitality sector to be supported by stable visitor arrivals and a pipeline of MICE and high-profile entertainment events.

"However, the operating environment remains challenging amid global uncertainties, manpower constraints and rising costs," the company said.

Against this backdrop, it is scheduled to open the first NoMad hotel in the Asia Pacific region , along Orchard Road in Singapore, in late 2026.

The hotel has obtained its temporary occupation permit, UOL said on Aug 12.

The 19-storey luxury lifestyle hotel will comprise 173 rooms as well as curated commercial and retail offerings. It is situated at the former Faber House , which was an eight-storey commercial building sitting across the road from 313@somerset.

Liam had said earlier that NoMad Hilton Singapore is a key part of UOL’s placemaking vision for Orchard Road, alongside its luxury residential project UpperHouse at Orchard Boulevard and the Pan Pacific Orchard hotel.

Greater share of profit from JVs, higher revenue from property investments

Group revenue for the first half of the year fell 7% y-o-y to $1.44 billion on lower revenue from property development.

However, UOL clarified that this was because the group entered into more development projects through JVs — such as those for ParkTown Residence and Skye at Holland, which were launched in February and October 2025 respectively.

In fact, those joint venture development projects resulted in a significant y-o-y increase of $83.7 million in the group’s share of profit from JV companies in the half-year period.

That in turn contributed to a $53.8 million increase in pre-tax profit before fair value and other gains as compared to a year ago.

Revenue from property investments increased 4% to $316.7 million. It was driven by higher contributions from Singapore Land Tower and West Mall — both of which completed asset enhancement initiatives in 2025 — and from Varley Park in Brighton, UK, which was acquired in August 2025.

This was partly offset by the disposal of KINEX mall in Singapore last October.

title: US launches effort to speed trade in AI goods between allies
article:
(Aug 12): The Trump administration announced a new programme aimed at accelerating shipments between the US and its closest trading partners of goods considered critical to developing artificial intelligence.

The State Department said Wednesday that it will create a pilot platform in Panama intended to fast-track trade in products essential to AI as part of Pax Silica, a US-led initiative created to strengthen supply chains between allies. In a statement, the agency said it’s committing up to US$50 million in foreign assistance funding to develop and deploy the platform, which will use AI technology to speed the logistics process.

“The project is expected to accelerate logistics and compliance operations,” Under Secretary of State for Economic Affairs Jacob Helberg said in an email. “This project is focused on enabling Panama and other participating economies to track and expedite shipments from trusted suppliers of high-value cargo for AI infrastructure, semiconductors and critical minerals across the entire AI supply chain.”

The announcement marks the latest US move to strengthen its supply chains with allies and reduce their reliance on China for crucial materials used in AI and other advanced technologies. The Biden administration also launched initiatives, including the Minerals Security Partnership, aimed at loosening Beijing’s grip on the crucial sector — though no US effort so far has had a meaningful impact on China’s dominance.

Earlier this year, the Trump administration said that it would contribute as much as US$250 million toward a consortium to help fund projects aimed at boosting access to energy and critical minerals — two sectors that the president has repeatedly highlighted as key national security concerns.

Shippers use a combination of traditional pen-and-paper record-keeping alongside digital systems to track goods at ports of entry, costing the US government and foreign allies significant time and money. With the rising need to closely monitor custody of sensitive technology and intellectual property that officials and experts worry could fall into adversaries’ hands, the US is hoping AI-assisted technology can begin to replace conventional tracking methods.

See also: Tencent’s WorkBuddy sparks AI turnaround hopes after stock rout

Panama is a vital global shipping artery, with roughly 3% of all global maritime trade passing through its canal connecting the Atlantic and Pacific Oceans. Helberg said that Panama was chosen as the site of the pilot project following his visit there in May and based on strong interest from the country’s government.

The Pax Silica programme has roughly two dozen participants, including the European Union, the UK, India and the United Arab Emirates.

title: US stocks rise as inflation keeps Fed ‘at bay’, spurs tech rally
article:
(Aug 12): US stocks traded higher after a subdued inflation reading helped ease pressure on the Federal Reserve (Fed) to raise interest rates, clearing the way for an earnings-led tech rally to continue.

The S&P 500 rose 0.3% as of 10.30am in New York. The technology-heavy Nasdaq 100 rallied 1%, reversing its losses from earlier in the week. Tech is leading markets higher after Coreweave Inc, a bellwether for the data centre boom, and Super Micro Computer Inc reported earnings late Tuesday that affirmed confidence in the AI trade. Shares of Coreweave rose as much as 24% while Super Micro gained nearly 18% in early trading.

US CPI data released just ahead of the bell showed July consumer prices rose in line with expectations. Core inflation, which excludes volatile food and energy, advanced 2.5% on an annual basis, matching the slowest pace since March 2021.

July’s CPI reading and a cooler-than-expected jobs report “may keep hawkish Fed officials at bay in September”, said Gary Schlossberg, global strategist at Wells Fargo Investment Institute. “However, we remain guarded on the near-term outlook for inflation amid volatile oil prices tied to the ongoing Middle East conflict along with lingering core price pressures from a strong economy and the AI boom.”

PPI data, to be released Thursday, will allow markets to “get a better gauge of how this all passes into core PCE, the Fed’s preferred inflation measure”, said Molly Brooks, an analyst at TD Cowen.

“Overall, the print is supportive of a Fed hold, but we are not out of the woods on a hike as the Fed does not need much to tip them over the edge towards raising rates,” she said.

See also: CoreWeave shares soar after booming AI demand boosts outlook

A September rate decision is “likely to be more influenced by the combination of August’s jobs and inflation data”, said Josh Jamner, senior investment strategy analyst at ClearBridge Investments.

Market pricing of a Fed rate hike has pared to around 39%, after sitting at a 50-50 toss-up ahead of the print.

Dr Brian Jacobsen, chief economist at Annex Wealth Management LLC noted that there are still “pockets of extreme price pressure”. Computer software and accessories saw a 21.2% year-over-year increase, soaring amid the AI boom. Grocery prices have risen for three months, especially beef, eggs and dairy.

See also: US stocks waver near record as oil retreats ahead of inflation

Among July CPI highlights, Owner’s Equivalent Rent “remained tame”, according to John Kerschner, portfolio manager and head of securitised products at Janus Henderson Global. “Housing remains one of the brightest lights in the Fed’s fight against overall inflation, and we expect this to continue in the months ahead given mortgage rates stubbornly high,” he said.

Kerschner also pointed to a lower vehicle insurance print on the report, “as high insurance increases post-Covid continued to normalise”, as well as lettuce falling more than 16% after the recent Cyclospora outbreak weakened demand.

Brent crude oil is hovering around US$89 per barrel Wednesday as Strait of Hormuz negotiations remain in deadlock.

In single stock moves, Cava Group Inc shares climbed as much as 18%, the most intraday since February, after the restaurant chain reported faster than expected sales, with customers drawn in by their higher-priced offerings.

Traders will hear from Cisco Systems, Inc after the bell. The world’s largest maker of networking equipment is scheduled to report second quarter earnings that could provide an update on its push to capitalise on AI spending.
• Restaurants are in focus after strong earnings from Cava and Brinker, owner of Chili’s and Maggiano’s.
• Optical equipment stocks gain with Lumentum after it reported fourth-quarter results that beat expectations and gave an outlook above analyst consensus. Lumentum and its peers have been on a scorching run since last July.

title: AEM’s net profit rockets 876% y-o-y to $30.8 mil for 1H; guides higher FY2026 revenue of $630 mil to $680 mil
article:
For 1HFY2026 ended June 30, AEM Holdings reported a 876% y-o-y increase to $30.8 million, on revenue of $247 million, which is 29.9% higher than 1HFY2025. An interim dividend of 2.4 cents has been declared.

The better performance was attributed to a 191.7% y-o-y rise in revenue from AEM’s fabless artificial intelligence/ high performance computing (AI/ HPC) customer and a higher contribution from test cells solutions (TCS). On a sequential basis, revenue rose 11.5% q-o-q, supported by demand for solutions used in high-power AI and HPC device applications.

Net profit margin rose to 12.5%, up from 1HFY2025’s 1.7%. AEM says that the improvement was supported by a more favorable revenue mix driven by higher TCS contribution, better fixed-cost absorption at higher volumes, and greater operating leverage.

On a segmental basis, revenue from the TCS segment grew 52.5% y-o-y to $180.9 million which represented 73.2% of revenue. Growth was led by the deployment of AEM’s test solutions for advanced AI/ HPC applications, where demand is “intensifying” for highly parallel test solutions featuring “leading” thermal-control capabilities.

The contract manufacturing segment reported external revenue of $63.2 million, representing 25.6% of total revenue. External revenue decreased 5.7% y-o-y, mainly due to softer external demand from oil and gas customers.

AEM held cash and cash equivalents of $82.7 million with borrowings of $26.1 million. AEM says that its balance sheet provides business with the financial flexibility to support customer programme ramps, ongoing R&D initiatives and capital allocation priorities.

See also: Riverstone’s 2QFY2026 net profit up 60.2% y-o-y to RM65.8 mil, declares interim dividend of 5 sen

AEM has raised its FY2026 revenue guidance to $630 million to $680 million from $550 million to $600 million. The upward revision is supported by the production ramp-up of its fabless AI / HPC customer, the PC / Foundry customer’s adoption of the AMPS platform for future test requirements, and the planned shipment of the first memory final test handler in 4Q2026 ahead of a ramp in 2027. AEM guides full-year EPS to range from 24.5 to 27.5 cents.

AEM CEO Samer Kabbani says that the revenue and earnings growth reflects the strength of the company’s offerings. “As devices become more complex, more power dense, and harder to test, customers are increasingly focused on optimising the cost of test and are turning to precise thermal control, highly parallel testing, and full-stack integration – capabilities in which AEM holds a competitive advantage.”

Kabbani adds that AEM is advancing its growth strategy across five pillars — PC/foundry, AI/HPC, memory, outsourced semiconductor assembly and test (OSAT), and contract manufacturing. “With meaningful contributions from the first two pillars and our long-term partnership with ASE, AEM is well positioned to drive growth through the remainder of 2026 and beyond.”

Shares in AEM closed nine cents or 0.9% higher at $9.63 on Aug 12. Ytd, the counter has shot up by 453%. The interim dividend will be paid on Sept 8.

title: Thailand reaffirms US military cooperation amid trade talks
article:
(Aug 12): Thailand reaffirmed its longstanding military relationship with the US on Wednesday, saying security cooperation will remain separate from ongoing negotiations over US tariffs and will not be used as leverage in the talks.

Rachada Dhanadirek, a spokesperson for the government, said Thailand is carefully assessing proposals in the trade negotiations while seeking an agreement that delivers equitable benefits for both sides. Thailand’s security and military cooperation with the US is a longstanding relationship based on shared security interests, she said in a statement.

Bloomberg News reported on Tuesday that Bangkok was preparing to warn the Trump administration that steep US tariffs could force it to scale back military cooperation, including joint exercises, according to an official familiar with the matter. The position was expected to form part of a Thai counterproposal as reciprocal-trade negotiations resume later this month, the official said.

Rachada denied that the government would use military and security cooperation as a bargaining chip in the talks. Existing military programmes are on track, including the annual Cobra Gold joint exercise, she said.

“Thailand and the United States share broad and deep ties across many areas, including the economy, trade, security and people-to-people relations,” Rachada said. “Each area has its own framework and national interests that must be carefully considered. The government will not trade one national interest for another.”

title: Super Micro gives sales outlook that tops rosiest projection
article:
(Aug 12): Super Micro Computer Inc shares jumped after the company gave a revenue forecast for the current quarter that topped analysts’ estimates, a sign the booming artificial intelligence market continues to bolster sales of the company’s servers.

Revenue will be US$14.5 billion to US$15.5 billion in the period ending in September, the company said Tuesday in a statement. Profit, excluding some items, will be US$1.01 to US$1.10 a share. Analysts polled by Bloomberg projected sales, on average, of US$12 billion and profit of 74 cents. The outlook topped even the highest analyst revenue estimate of US$13.3 billion.

San Jose, California-based Super Micro is benefiting from surging demand for gear to train and run AI tasks. The company’s servers are fitted with the Nvidia Corp chips that have become the workhorse for the vast majority of AI data centres. Super Micro has also been working to boost margins by selling more profitable products and trimming costs.

“Combined with continued investment in technology leadership, manufacturing scale and global compliance, we are enabling customers to deploy AI infrastructure faster and more efficiently,” CEO Charles Liang said in the statement.

The shares surged as much as 18% to US$37.13 after markets opened in New York on Wednesday. The stock was already up 8% this year through Tuesday’s close.

Last month, the company’s shares rose 20% in a single day after the server maker issued preliminary fiscal fourth-quarter results saying its backlog hit a record on new orders of more than US$60 billion. The company also said margins would be better than forecast.

See also: Nvidia partner Hon Hai scores profit beat on AI spending surge

On Tuesday, Super Micro said revenue will be US$65 billion to US$72 billion in the fiscal year that began in July. Analysts, on average, projected US$54.4 billion.

The annual outlook “reflects strengthening AI opportunities and sales execution, with modest improvement in normalised gross margin,” Bloomberg Intelligence analyst Woo Jin Ho said in a note.

In March, US prosecutors charged Super Micro co-founder Yih-Shyan “Wally” Liaw with illegally diverting billions of dollars in Nvidia-powered servers to China, in violation of US export controls. Super Micro isn’t named as a defendant and the company has said it’s cooperating with authorities. In late June, Taiwanese prosecutors detained two Super Micro employees following a raid of the company’s local offices.

See also: Nvidia partner Hon Hai’s sales rise 54% on strong AI demand

In the quarter that ended June 30, Super Micro reported sales climbed 93% to US$11.1 billion and profit, excluding some items, was US$1.70 a share. Analysts, on average, estimated sales of US$11.3 billion and earnings of US$1.59 a share. Adjusted gross margin was 17.6%.

title: Reclaims Global secures $19.89 mil in new contracts in 2QFY2026
article:
Reclaims Global Limited (Reclaims Global) (SGX:NEX ) announced that it has secured multiple new contracts with an aggregate value of around $19.89 million awarded from various public and private sector clients in 2QFY2026.

Reclaims Global says that the new contracts comprise a wide range of services, including excavation and earthworks, demolition and disposal work, reinstatement works, pilehead disposal services, temporary hoarding installation, environmental services, logistics support, and related site enabling works.

“Supported by a resilient construction outlook in Singapore, we remain focused on disciplined project execution, operational excellence, and selectively pursuing quality opportunities that drive sustainable long-term growth,” says Tan Kok Huat, executive director and CEO of Reclaims Global.

Barring any unforeseen circumstances, Reclaims Global expects the new contracts to contribute positively to its net tangible assets and earnings per share throughout the duration of the projects.

Shares of Reclaims Global closed unchanged at 21.5 cents on Aug 12.

title: Penguin International reports 30.1% y-o-y net profit jump to $9.14 mil for 1HFY2026
article:
For 1HFY2026, Mainboard-listed Penguin International has reported a 30.1% rise in net profit to $9.14 million on revenue of $137.4 million which is 12.6% higher than 1HFY2025. No interim dividend was declared as Penguin intends to conserve cash for its fleet and shipyard expansion projects.

Gross profit improved 19% to $47.2 million while cost of sales increased by 9.5% y-o-y to $90.2 million. Administrative expenses rose 30.3% to $23.3 million and was more than offset by a 46.2% y-o-y decrease in other operating expenses to $8.5 million.

Segmentally, revenue from ship chartering jumped 111% to $54.3 million while revenue from shipyard activities declined nearly 14% to $83.1 million.

The company owned cash holdings of $13.8 million as at June 30, a decrease from $30.8 million as at Dec 31. The reduction in cash balances reflects planned investments in fleet and shipyard capacity, dividends and scheduled debt repayment, rather than a deterioration in operating cash generation.

Bank borrowings amounted to $49 million as at June 30, as the company paid back around $5.9 million during 1HFY2026.

During the period, the Group chartered four of its Flex Fighter armoured security vessels to the Australian Border Force for border protection. It also delivered the first of six carbon fibre composite superstructures for the Republic of Singapore Navy's Multi-Role Combat Vessel programme.

See also: Food Empire posts record 1HFY2026 NPAT of US$35.3 mil; declares dividend of 4 cents per share

Penguin also partially monetised its investment in Marco Polo Marine and redeployed $17.4 million into its core designer-builder-owner-operator platform. The company remains confident in Marco Polo Marine's management team and long-term prospects.

The company also believes that shipbuilding, maintenance and vessel chartering services remains healthy across its four primary markets in offshore oil and gas/ maritime security; government; offshore wind; and tourism.

Demand for Penguin’s multi-role crewboats and armoured security vessels is expected to remain “firm” over the next 12 months, supported by ongoing offshore oil and gas activities, maritime security needs and fleet renewal requirements.

See also: Hong Leong Asia’s 1HFY2026 earnings up by 64.1% to $91.9 mil; declares dividend of 3 cents per share

Meanwhile, the firm continues to capture opportunities in government and maritime security markets through both vessel operations and shipbuilding with 46% of shipbuilding, ship repair and maintenance revenue in 1HFY2026 generated from government. This compares with the 25% in the previous corresponding period.

Penguin says that the offshore wind sector is showing signs of recovery, following a period of slower activity, as a growing number of European projects move from planning into construction, installation and operational phases. At the same time, demand for ferries and RoPaxes remains supported by fleet renewal requirements, environmental regulations and rising tourist arrivals in key markets.

Shares in Penguin remained flat at $1.50 on Aug 12.

title: COSCO patmi surges 188% y-o-y to $7.57 million for 1HFY2026
article:
For 1HFY2026, COSCO Shipping International reported a 188% increase in patmi to $7.57 million, on revenue of $96.8 million, which is 6% higher than 1HFY2025. No interim dividend was declared as the company is evaluating strategic business expansion to ensure sustainable growth.

Gross profit increased 3% y-o-y to $23.8 million while cost of sales increased 8% y-o-y to $73 million, in line with the increase in revenue from warehousing services, automotive services and ship repair and marine engineering. Profit for the period rose 149% y-o-y to $8.28 million.

On a segmental basis, revenue from logistics activities increased 6% y-o-y to $85.2 million mainly due to higher revenue from warehousing services and automotive services. The logistics segment accounts for about 88% of COSCO’s revenue in 1HFY2026.

For property management, revenue 1% y-o-y from to $1.27 million, mainly due to the increase in revenue from rental and service fee. Revenue from ship repair and marine engineering increased by 14% y-o-y to nearly $10.4 million, mainly due to higher revenue from ship repair and fabrication works.

Cash and cash equivalents decreased from $179.0 million to $153.9 million, mainly due to acquisitions of property, plant and equipment, offset by net cash provided by operating activities. Borrowings decreased 1% to around $92.7 million.

The net proceeds from a July 2025 rights issue have substantially been deployed towards the development of Jurong Island Logistics Hub (JILH) phase II and the repayment of bank borrowings. The company says the new capital has “strengthened” its capital structure and financial flexibility, enabling the business to support its long-term growth objectives and ongoing investment needs amid an uncertain external environment.

See also: Hong Leong Asia’s 1HFY2026 earnings up by 64.1% to $91.9 mil; declares dividend of 3 cents per share

COSCO also updated that it expects to obtain the temporary occupation permit for JILH phase II by the end of the year. It adds that it continues to advance the restructuring and integration of its logistics operations in Malaysia to streamline its business structure, enhance operational efficiency and optimise costs.

Shares in COSCO closed at 11.9 cents on Aug 12, down 0.2 cents or 1.7%.
